fund_001:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare Y Combinator-style SAFE documents for our pre-seed raise using {{vendor}}, our legal-ops document automation platform. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) my company's legal name, state of incorporation, and signer name/title; (2) the SAFE type we're using (post-money, valuation cap and/or discount, MFN, or pro-rata rights); (3) the target valuation cap and discount percentage; (4) a list of prospective investor names and entities; and (5) my {{vendor}} account/workspace details if there are multiple templates or workflows to choose from.

Using your configured credentials, do the following: log into {{vendor}} (or use its API) to locate the standard YC SAFE template, complete the guided questionnaire with the details I provide, and generate a populated SAFE document for each investor. Flag any questionnaire choices or non-standard terms that the tool marks as needing attorney review, and list them clearly. If {{vendor}} supports programmatic document generation, launch the appropriate workflow/API call to create each SAFE document from the template rather than drafting from scratch.

Do not send documents for signature, submit them, or finalize anything — this step requires my explicit approval before any changes are applied. Prepare a summary showing: each investor name, the SAFE terms populated, any flagged review items, and links or references to the generated draft documents in {{vendor}}. Then stop for human sign-off, clearly stating that you are waiting for my review and approval before proceeding to send or execute any SAFE.

fund_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me set up an investor pipeline tracker for our pre-seed SAFE fundraise using {{vendor}}, our project-management tool. If you don't already have it, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} workspace/team details, (2) the list of target investor names, firms, and any known contact info I want pre-loaded, and (3) the pipeline stages I want to track (e.g., Sourced, Contacted, Meeting Scheduled, Pitched, Due Diligence, Committed, Passed, Closed).

Using your configured credentials, do the following via {{vendor}}'s API:
1. Create a pipeline tracker structure (a list or database) dedicated to this fundraise.
2. Customize fields to match our process: investor name, firm, contact, check size/target, stage/status, last contact date, next follow-up date, and notes.
3. For each investor I provide, create a task (using the create-task API) capturing their details, current stage, and — where relevant — a due date for the next follow-up action, assigned to me.
4. Create at least one view (using the create-view API) to organize and visualize the pipeline by stage, and if supported, set up a board view for stage-based tracking and a list or timeline view for follow-up dates.
5. Confirm the tracker supports multiple view types (board, list, calendar/timeline) so we can review pipeline health different ways.

When done, report back: the tracker/database name and location in {{vendor}}, the field/stage schema you configured, the number of investor tasks created (with a sample of 2-3), the views created, and any investors from my list you couldn't add (with reasons). Flag any API limitations you hit so I can adjust manually if needed.

fund_001:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare draft outreach emails for our pre-seed fundraise using YC SAFEs. Use {{vendor}} (our configured AI assistant) to draft these, working from investor and company details I provide.

First, ask me for anything missing: (1) our company one-liner and stage, (2) round size/terms context (e.g., valuation cap, discount if any), (3) a list of target investors with names, firms, and any personalization notes (how we know them, mutual connections, relevant portfolio fit), (4) any existing deck or one-pager link to reference, and (5) my preferred tone (warm intro vs cold outreach) and sender name/signature.

Then, using {{vendor}}, draft a distinct outreach email for each investor: a short, compelling subject line; a 3-5 sentence body covering who we are, traction/problem-solution fit, why this investor specifically, and a clear ask (e.g., 15-minute call); and a signature block. Iterate on tone and length based on my feedback until I approve the drafts. Save all drafts as a single document (or export file) organized by investor name so I can review them together.

Do not send any emails yet — sending requires explicit human approval. If I later ask you to send an approved draft, use the email API's send-message operation with our configured credentials, but only after I have approved that specific draft.

When done, report back: number of drafts created, the document/file location, and a short list of any investors where you lacked enough context to personalize the email, so I can supply details. Then stop for human sign-off before any sending occurs.

fund_001:n5.prompt:
You are helping me manage logistics around investor meetings for my pre-seed SAFE fundraise. The actual meetings (relationship-building, pitching, and real-time negotiation) are conversations I must conduct myself — this remains a human step you cannot perform. Your job is to prepare and track everything around those meetings.

First, ask me for anything you need: my target investor list (names, firms, emails), my pitch deck link or file, my data room link, my calendar availability, and any CRM or spreadsheet I already use to track outreach (e.g., Google Sheets, Airtable, Notion).

Then do the following:
1. Build or update a tracker (spreadsheet or doc) listing each investor with columns for: contact info, meeting status (not scheduled / scheduled / completed / follow-up sent), meeting date, notes, and next action.
2. Draft personalized meeting confirmation emails and follow-up/thank-you emails for each investor, referencing their firm and any prior context I give you, ready for me to review and send.
3. Prepare a pre-meeting briefing note for each scheduled meeting summarizing the investor's background, focus areas, and suggested talking points based on public information I provide or that you can find.
4. Set up reminders or a checklist for me to poll: after each meeting date passes, prompt me to log the outcome and any next steps (e.g., send SAFE terms, schedule follow-up, decline).

Done looks like: a complete, up-to-date investor meeting tracker, drafted emails ready for my review, briefing notes for upcoming meetings, and a polling checklist so I remember to update statuses after each meeting occurs.

Report back with: the tracker link/location, a summary of drafted emails awaiting my send approval, and a list of meetings still needing status updates from me. Do not attempt to conduct, join, or simulate the investor conversations themselves — only prepare materials and track status.

fund_001:n6.prompt:
You are helping me send our Y Combinator SAFE notes out for e-signature as part of closing our pre-seed round. Use {{vendor}}, our legal-ops e-signature platform, accessed via my already-configured credentials.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: the finalized SAFE document(s) or template, the list of signers (investor name, email, and signing role/order for each, plus my own founder signature block), and any per-investor variables (investment amount, valuation cap or discount, entity name).

Then, using {{vendor}}'s document API or dashboard:
1. Generate/populate each SAFE with the correct investor name, amount, and terms.
2. Assemble the signature envelope with the correct recipients and routing order (investor signs, then founder countersigns, or per our standard order).
3. If {{vendor}} supports it, create a notarization request for the SAFE via the notarization API (create a notarization request through the operation described, e.g. POST /notarization) — only if we require notarized signatures for this round.
4. Prepare a summary for each envelope: investor name, amount, cap/discount, recipient emails, and routing order, plus a preview or link to the populated document for my review.

Do NOT click send, submit, or finalize the envelope yourself. Present me with the fully prepared envelopes and summaries and then stop for human sign-off — I will review the terms and recipient list and manually trigger the actual send.

Report back with: the list of prepared envelopes (one per investor), the terms populated into each, confirmation that recipients and routing order are correct, any notarization requests created, and a clear note that everything is staged and awaiting my approval to send.

fund_001:n7.prompt:
You are helping me close my pre-seed round, raised on Y Combinator SAFEs. Your job in this step is to verify that the wire transfers from investors who signed SAFEs have actually arrived in my company's {{vendor}} business bank account. Then reconcile them against what each investor committed.

Inputs to ask me for if you don't already have them:
- The list of signed SAFEs: investor name or entity, committed amount, and signing date. A spreadsheet or cap table export is fine.
- Which {{vendor}} account is receiving the funds, if I have more than one.
- The date range to check. Default to the earliest SAFE signing date through today.

Actions:
1. Use your configured credentials to connect to {{vendor}} through its documented public API.
2. List my business accounts and identify the one receiving the SAFE wires.
3. Pull incoming transactions for that account over the date range. Focus on incoming wires and other inbound deposits. If helpful, check the daily balance history to confirm the deposits posted.
4. Match each incoming wire to a SAFE investor. Use sender name, amount and date. Flag partial matches, such as an amount net of bank fees or a sender name that differs because funds came from a fund entity or LLC.
5. If {{vendor}} supports webhooks for incoming transactions, tell me whether a subscription would let us catch the remaining wires automatically. Do not create one without asking me.

This is read-only. Do not initiate, return or move any funds.

Done looks like this: every signed SAFE is marked one of the following:
- **Received**, with the matching transaction date and amount
- **Mismatch**, with the discrepancy explained
- **Not yet received**

Report back with:
- A table with these columns: investor, committed amount, received amount, date received, transaction reference, status.
- Totals for committed, received and outstanding.
- A short list of investors I should follow up with, and why.
- Any incoming wires you could not match to a SAFE.

fund_001:n8.prompt:
You are helping me update our cap table in {{vendor}} (our equity-management platform) to record a new SAFE issuance from our pre-seed raise. 

Before starting, ask me for anything you need: our {{vendor}} issuer ID, the investor name(s), the SAFE amount(s), valuation cap/discount terms, and confirmation that the SAFE documents are fully executed.

Steps to perform:
1. Use the configured credentials to call {{vendor}}'s capitalization-table endpoint (GET /v1alpha1/issuers/{issuer_id}/capitalization-table) to pull the current cap table by share class, and the stakeholders endpoint (GET /v1alpha1/issuers/{issuer_id}/stakeholders) to list current stakeholders.
2. Reconcile this data against our existing data room records — flag any mismatches in stakeholder names, share counts, or outstanding SAFEs before proceeding.
3. Prepare a draft entry for the new SAFE(s): investor name, investment amount, cap/discount terms, and how it should model into the cap table's conversion terms upon a future priced round.
4. Produce a clear summary showing: (a) the current cap table state, (b) the proposed new SAFE entry/entries, and (c) the resulting pro-forma ownership picture if the SAFEs were converted at the cap.
5. Do NOT submit, finalize, or apply the SAFE entry into {{vendor}}'s live cap table. This step requires a human to explicitly approve before any changes are applied — stop for human sign-off once your draft summary and reconciliation are ready.

Report back with: the reconciliation results (any discrepancies found), the full draft SAFE entry details ready for entry, and the pro-forma ownership summary. Clearly state that you are pausing for my explicit approval before any data is written to the live cap table, and specify exactly what action you will take once I approve.

fund_001:n9.prompt: You are helping me prepare (but NOT submit) our SEC Form D filing for our pre-seed SAFE round, required within 15 days of the first sale of securities. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) our legal entity name, EIN, state/jurisdiction and date of incorporation, (2) principal office address, (3) names/addresses of executive officers, directors, and any promoters, (4) the date of first sale in this offering, (5) total offering amount and amount sold to date, (6) number of investors and whether any are non-accredited, (7) the exemption being claimed (Rule 506(b) or 506(c)), (8) our EDGAR/SEC filer credentials status (use your configured credentials if you have programmatic access; otherwise note that a human will log in manually), and (9) the name and title of the authorized signer who will certify the filing. Using this information, draft a complete Form D data set formatted exactly as required by the SEC's EDGAR online filing system at https://www.onlineforms.edgarfiling.sec.gov/, including all issuer information, offering details, and related persons. Organize this into a clear checklist/summary document so the authorized signer can review every field before submission. Do not log in, enter data into EDGAR, certify, sign, or submit the filing yourself — filing Form D requires an authorized company representative to legally attest to the disclosures, so you must stop for human sign-off once the draft and checklist are ready. Report back with: the completed draft Form D field-by-field summary, any missing or ambiguous information you need from me, and a short list of final verification steps for the human filer to complete before they submit.

fund_001:n10.prompt:
You are helping me send the closing confirmation email for my YC SAFE pre-seed round to all participating investors, using {{vendor}} as the email tool. Before drafting, ask me for anything you need that's missing: the list of investor names and email addresses, the round details (SAFE type, valuation cap/discount, total amount raised, closing date), a link or reference to the signed SAFE documents, and the sender inbox/account you should use with {{vendor}}.

Once you have this, draft a clear, professional closing confirmation email that: thanks the investor, confirms their specific investment amount and SAFE terms, states the official closing date, references where signed documents and wire instructions live (or confirms funds received if applicable), and gives a point of contact for questions. Personalize each draft per investor rather than sending one generic blast.

Prepare these drafts as individual messages ready to send via {{vendor}}'s documented API or connected inbox access (e.g., composing and queuing send-message calls), but do NOT actually send anything yet. Show me the full list of recipients with their personalized draft text, the sender address, and a summary of round details being confirmed, so I can review for accuracy before anything goes out. Because a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied, you must stop for human sign-off after presenting the drafts — do not send, submit, or dispatch any email yourself.

When done, report back with: the number of investor drafts prepared, the {{vendor}} inbox/account used, a copy of each draft for my review, and a note confirming everything is staged and awaiting my explicit approval to send.
